question: Should exact requester consumption count as durable descendant delivery when the requester’s final outward channel send later fails?
rationale: The patch intentionally changes the terminal delivery boundary and suppresses later descendant retry; tests can prove implementation mechanics but cannot decide whether that user-visible reliability tradeoff is the desired product contract.

options.title: Accept requester consumption
options.body: Treat exact consumed run IDs as delivered after fixing canonical task targeting and adding live restart proof.

options.title: Require outward delivery
options.body: Credit descendants only after the requester result is successfully delivered to its final channel, preserving retries when that send fails.

options.title: Fold into durable inbox
options.body: Pause this PR and handle requester consumption within the broader durable completion inbox or spool design.

recommendation.title: Accept requester consumption
recommendation.body: Treat exact consumed run IDs as delivered after fixing canonical task targeting and adding live restart proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available routing candidate across the current task-ledger, subagent lifecycle, and persisted registry boundaries involved in this choice.
